# Research question

## Main question:

> What drives tipping behavior in restaurants

## Subquestions:

- Q1 \[`dplyr`\]: What are the average and median tip amounts and what proportion of customers leave a tip of at least 20%?

- Q2 \[`dplyr`\]: Which parties (f. ex. smoking women) tipped highest and which the lowest?

- Q3 \[`dplyr`\]: How do lunch and dinner compare on average bill, tip and number of parties?

- Q4 \[`dplyr`\]: For each shift (day × time), how many tables were served, and what was the average tip and tip %? Which shift is busiest, and which is most generous?

- Q5 \[`ggplot2`\]: What is the relationship between the total bill amount and the tip amount?

- Q6 \[`ggplot2`\]: Where should the waiter want to be? Heatmap (geom_tile) of average tip by day × size, or a bar chart of average tip by day, filled by smoker?

- Q7 \[`ggplot2`\]: Do tips and tip percentages differ between days of the week and between lunch and dinner?

- Q8 \[`ggplot2`\]: Are smokers really less predictable tippers than non-smokers?

# Dataset

The dataset that we use is a `tips` dataset. It is available on kaggle.com (<https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/saurabhbadole/restaurant-tips-dataset>).

| feature           | short description                      |
|:------------------|:---------------------------------------|
| number of rows    | $244$                                  |
| number of columns | $7$                                    |
| key variables     | `total_bill`, `tip`                    |
| other variables   | `sex`, `smoker`, `day`, `time`, `size` |
| missing values    | None                                   |
| cleaning          | None                                   |

# Analysis

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

tips <- read_csv("tips.csv")
```

```{r}
glimpse(tips)
```

```{r}
head(tips)
```

### dplyr

> Q1: What are the average and median tip amounts and what proportion of customers leave a tip of at least 20%?

```{r}
tips<-tips |> 
  mutate(percentage=round(100*tip/total_bill))

tips|> 
  summarize(
    mean_tip                = round(mean(tip),2),
    median_tip              = round(median(tip),2),
    mean_tip_percentage     = round(mean(percentage)),
    median_tip_percentage   = round(median(percentage)),
    pctg_of_tips_above_20p  = round(100 * sum(percentage > 20) / n())
  )
```

> Q2: Which parties (f. ex. smoking women) tipped highest and which the lowest?

```{r}
tips <- tips |>
  mutate(percent_tip = tip / (tip + total_bill) * 100) 

tips |>
  group_by(sex, smoker) |>
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    mean_tip       = round(mean(tip), 2),
    median_tip     = round(median(tip), 2),
    mean_tip_pct   = round(mean(percent_tip), 2),
    median_tip_pct = round(median(percent_tip), 2),
    sd_tip_pct     = round(sd(percent_tip), 2),
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_tip))
```

> Q3: How do lunch and dinner compare on average bill, tip and number of parties?

```{r}
tips |>
  mutate(
    bill_per_person = total_bill / size,
    tip_per_person = tip / size,
    tip_percentage = tip / total_bill * 100,
  ) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    n_parties   = n(),
    avg_bill_pp = round(mean(bill_per_person), 2),
    avg_tip_pp  = round(mean(tip_per_person), 2),
    avg_bill    = round(mean(total_bill), 2),
    median_bill = round(median(total_bill), 2),
    avg_tip     = round(mean(tip), 2),
    median_tip  = round(median(tip), 2),
    avg_tip_pct = round(mean(tip_percentage), 2),
  ) |>
  arrange(
    case_when(
      time == "Lunch"  ~ 1,
      time == "Dinner" ~ 2,
      .default = 9
    )
  )
```

> Q4: For each shift (day × time), how many tables were served, and what was the average tip and tip %? Which shift is busiest, and which is most generous?

### ggplot2

> Q5: What is the relationship between the total bill amount and the tip amount?

```{r}
tips|> 
  ggplot(
    aes(x=total_bill,y=percentage)
  )+
  geom_point(
    aes(color=factor(sex)),  alpha=0.5
  )+
  geom_smooth()+
  labs(
    title = "Tip percentage as a function of the total bill",
    x = "Total bill [USD]",
    y = "Tip percentage [%]",
    color = "Sex"
  )+
  theme_minimal()
```

> Q6: Where should the waiter want to be? Heatmap (geom_tile) of average tip by day × size, or a bar chart of average tip by day, filled by smoker?

> Q7: Do tips and tip percentages differ between days of the week and between lunch and dinner?

```{r}
tips <- tips |>
  mutate(
    tip_pct = tip / total_bill * 100,
    day  = factor(day,  levels = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")),
    time = factor(time, levels = c("Lunch", "Dinner"))
  )

tips |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(tip, tip_pct),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("tip", "tip_pct"),
      labels = c("Tip ($)", "Tip (% of bill)")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(x = day, y = value, fill = time)
  )+
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkorange", "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title = "Tip and tip percentage by day and meal time",
    subtitle = "Data: tips dataset",
    x = "Day",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Meal time"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

> Q8: Are smokers really less predictable tippers than non-smokers?

```{r}
group_medians <- tips |>
  group_by(sex, smoker) |>
  summarise(med_pct = median(percent_tip), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(tips, aes(x = percent_tip, fill = smoker)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_vline(
    data = group_medians,
    aes(xintercept = med_pct, color = smoker),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ sex) +
  # for x axis
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 45)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "darkorange", "Yes" = "steelblue")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("No" = "darkorange", "Yes" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Male group is more coherent than the female group",
    x        = "Tip Percentage (%)",
    y        = "Density",
    fill     = "Smoker",
    color    = "Smoker",
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Statistical Analysis

```{r}
library(car) 

# 1. Levene test - to check the variance equality
# Ho - equal variances
# H1 - different variances
leveneTest(percent_tip ~ smoker, data = tips)
# p < 0.05 -> NOT EQUAL!

# 2. Two-way ANOVA (check sex, smoker and mix significance)
anova_model <- aov(percent_tip ~ sex * smoker, data = tips)
summary(anova_model)
# sex:smoker Pr = 0.26 -> smoking effects women and man in a different way


# 3. Shapiro-Wilk test - checking the distribution of anova
shapiro.test(residuals(anova_model))
# tiny p-valy - it does not have a normal distribution

```
